title: Death comes on time, from Him, and never as an accident
subtitle: Al-Mumit: the One who causes death at its appointed time, with wisdom
intro: Al-Mumit (اَلْمُمِيتُ) means the Bringer of Death: the One who takes every soul at the exact time He has decreed, no earlier and no later, and who created death and life to test which of us does best. Death is not chaos or bad luck. Knowing this name turns fear of death into readiness, and grief into trust.

root.sense: Mawt is death, the end of life in a body, and imatah is causing death. The word is also used for land without plants and for a heart without faith. Al-Mumit is the One who decrees the end of each life, and sleep is described in the Quran as a lesser form of the same taking.

picture.label: Death in the hand of Al-Mumit

knowing: Scholars note that Al-Mumit is a name mentioned together with its pair, Al-Muhyi, and the Quran almost always puts them side by side: He gives life and causes death (57:2). {idea}Death is not a defeat of His power but an act of it{/idea}, as deliberate as birth. He created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deeds, and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving (67:2). The verse names death first, as part of the design, and closes with forgiveness.

No one shares this with Him. A king once argued with Ibrahim, claiming that he too gave life and death because he could spare one prisoner and execute another. Ibrahim answered: Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west. The man was left speechless (2:258). Human power can end a life by violence; only Allah decrees the term of every soul.

His timing is exact. When a term comes, no one can delay it by an hour or bring it forward (16:61). Wherever you are, death will reach you, even in towers built high (4:78). {trap}All the security, wealth and medicine in the world cannot move that moment{/trap}, and the most powerful people on earth discover at the end how little control they had.
seeing: Every night you rehearse it. Allah takes souls at their death, and those that have not died He takes in their sleep, then keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others back until a set time (39:42). You lie down, lose control of everything, and wake only because He returned you.

The Prophet ﷺ wept when his young son Ibrahim died, and said that the eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord, as recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari. When his daughter's child was dying, he sent her word that to Allah belongs what He takes and what He gives, and everything with Him has a fixed term, so let her be patient and hope for reward (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim). {reward}Grief is allowed; despair is not needed{/reward}.
trusting: After a death, the mind runs through every if only: if we had gone to a different hospital, if they had not taken that road. The Quran warns against this exact thought, saying such regret is turned into anguish in the heart, and that it is Allah who gives life and causes death (3:156). {idea}Their time was set by the Wise, not by your mistake{/idea}. You can let that guilt go.

Knowing Al-Mumit also changes how you live. If the time is fixed and unknown, the wise move is to be ready now: pay the debt, make the call, forgive the grudge, give the charity before you are left saying, my Lord, if only You would delay me a little (63:10). Fear turns into focus.
loving: For a believer, death is not falling into nothing but being taken by the One who made you and has cared for you all along. {reward}Al-Mumit is the One who brings you home{/reward}. The more you love Him, the less the door frightens you, because you know whose house is on the other side.
now: You are standing in a hospital corridor at 3am after the doctor's quiet words, replaying every decision you made this week. Breathe. Al-Mumit set this term long before you made a single choice, and He is the Forgiving. Say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we belong to Allah and to Him we return.
old: I see death as a cruel accident that someone could have prevented.
new: I see death as an appointment set by Al-Mumit, with wisdom, leading the believer to Him.
try: Do one thing today that you would want done if this were your last week: settle a small debt, call a parent, or forgive someone.

dua.text: O Allah, You are Al-Mumit. When You take my soul, take it while You are pleased with me, and make the best of my days the day I meet You.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name at a funeral or a deathbed, and when fear of death grips you, asking for a good ending rather than a longer delay.

pairs.why: He gives life and causes death; the two are named together throughout the Quran.
Death is not the end, because Al-Ba'ith raises everyone He caused to die.
Every creature dies at its term; only Al-Hayy lives forever and never dies.

faq.a: Al-Mumit means the One who causes death. Allah takes every soul at the time He decreed, with wisdom and without any mistake in timing. Scholars mention it together with its pair Al-Muhyi, the Giver of life.

The Quran says He created death and life to test which of us is best in deeds (67:2). Death closes the test, and then each soul is repaid in full on the Day of Resurrection (3:185). For believers, it is the doorway to meeting their Lord.

faq.q: Could a death have been prevented?
faq.a: We are told to take care, use medicine and avoid harm. But the Quran teaches that when a term comes it is neither delayed nor brought forward (16:61), and it warns against the if only regret that tortures the bereaved (3:156).
